statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 11% sits in the low band, well below the block threshold, for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD.
recommendation: Tail remains below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping yields EA_ON for both instruments. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 13:30-15:00 UTC window covering the U.S. cash open and the S&P Global flash PMIs, where the published forecast reaches the WATCH band for two hours, and again in the 19:00 UTC power hour. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Narrow, orderly overnight band under a record close keeps Tail at the low-band floor
body: The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,732.40, up 250.04 points or 0.82%, inside a 30,496.43-30,770.63 range and at a fresh 52-week and all-time closing high, with the Nasdaq Composite up 2.26% to a record on AI enthusiasm around Meta's Muse assistant, AMD passing a $1 trillion market capitalisation and broad semiconductor leadership. Globex NQ now trades 30,999.50, down 29.00 points or 0.09%, roughly 14 points above the 30,985.25 overnight low and inside an 85-point 30,985.25-31,070.50 band. That is an orderly retracement off the overnight high: no shallow-pullback chain, no repeated extension after a failed retracement and no holding of a session extreme has been observed since the reopen, which is why Tail stays at the low-band floor. VIX at 14.21 is down 4.44% and settled near its 14.19 session low. The latest H.15 observations put the 2-year at 4.76%, the 10-year at 4.96% and the 30-year at 5.29%, with the long end five basis points lower than the prior observation, so the rate backdrop is firm but no longer tightening into the tape. Crude fell for a sixth session, WTI near 89.66 and Brent near 98.83, after Saudi Arabia began restarting its East-West pipeline and Iran signalled a possible Strait of Hormuz reopening; that is a de-escalating energy and geopolitical channel rather than an amplifier. Cross-asset signals are therefore aligned toward calm rather than toward a no-retracement path. Shared Finviz context was collected at 00:58 UTC with partial status and both its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it is treated as stale, delayed, latest-session context only; its available breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections corroborate the chip-led prior-session tone and were not used as live price-path evidence. The scheduled stack for the coming session is light: S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45 UTC and EIA crude inventories at 14:30 UTC, with the jobless-claims block not until 12:30 UTC on 24 September. Stress at 34% reflects a record-high tape that can still swing widely, and Confidence at 87% reflects a live NQ quote, a verified cash close, current VIX, H.15 yields, crude levels and a verified calendar.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a previously published Claude assessment. Tail ranged from 11% to 21%, with the mapped state EA_ON in 21 hours and WATCH in three: the 14:00 UTC cash-session hour and the 18:00-19:00 UTC power-hour block on 22 September. Stress peaked at 46% around the cash open and decayed to 34% by the 01:00 and 02:00 UTC slots as the record close was absorbed, while Confidence held between 84% and 88% throughout. The dominant mode ran as normal through the Asian and European hours, shifted to trend-up and mixed across the U.S. cash session and the record close, and returned to normal in the most recent slot as the overnight fade proved orderly. No published hour reached the block threshold.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are expected to hold the low Tail band through the Asian and European sessions, with conditional risk concentrated in the 13:30-15:00 UTC block where the U.S. cash open and the S&P Global flash PMIs coincide, and again in the 19:00 UTC power hour after a record close. Three forecast hours reach the WATCH band on the scenario of a continuation leg that denies an early retracement; all three decay quickly in the published path, because Tail is scored down as soon as price discovery is orderly and retracements occur. No hour in the forecast reaches the block threshold. Published Confidence declines steadily from 87% to 76% purely as a function of distance from the observed evidence, not because of any identified deterioration.
